utterances.text: I think, to be most certain, that you would need to go back to the system and the process that the military used in order to send -- to send their reports, to number their reports, encrypt them and to send them. This is -- this was intended as an internal document based on information that one person had told another member of the team that I thought was worth recording, but it -- it looks like it was, you know, based on a memory of someone who had worked for 2 Corps that was speculating that such a thing was possible, three years after the dates had been sent -- or three days after the -- three years after the conversations had been recorded.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You interviewed or attended the interviews of a number of operators, interceptors. Do you remember any operator who said to you that the reports were not sent on the very same day upon which the conversations were intercepted?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that with the exception of the possibility being presented that if a conversation had been recorded late in a day that it might be sent the next morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: It's fairly logical that if a conversation is intercepted at 1159 the report would be sent the next day. However, on the basis of these notes, the conversations were sometimes sent months later. I have a question; I don't know whether you can answer it. But I'm wondering what was the usefulness of the work done by the interceptors intercepting those conversations if they stayed for months on the northern or the southern site and the command of the 2nd Corps could not see them or analyse them?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, I mean this is -- this is kind of a speculative comment, and the purpose of intercepting the communication was for operational purposes. So time was of the essence.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Earlier you were speaking about the floppy disks or the diskettes. You mentioned them several times. And you said that at the outset you were not able to open them, but finally they were opened and the OTP was able to take advantage of the information on those disks. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you know if those disks were the originals that were made at the time in 1995, or were they recordings of files that were made after the war?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding is that they were copies of files that were -- the copies were made after the war of files that were made during the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did you analyse the disks to know whether the content of the files had been modified? Did you carry out an expertise to that end?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: From a technical standpoint, no. In the last couple of months, when I've been working with this material again and I was introduced to the electronic versions of the printed material that we had received in 1998, I did have a chance to compare the content of those two bodies of material, if you want to call them that, and I didn't find any differences between them other than the fact that the electronic copies were more complete because they contained the headers and the dates and names and ...

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You referred to the printed matter. Are you referring to the material that was in those binders or the binder of 550 pages? Is that what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And you said earlier that indeed that material was compiled after the war by the members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It was prepared specifically for the OTP.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what my notes say.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And if we take each disk individually, you don't know whether it was modified after the war. And if you take each printout individually, you don't know if it was manipulated or modified after the war either.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: When you say no, does that mean you agree with what I just said?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we show the witness the Exhibit 5D158. I think it would be preferable not to broadcast this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please attend to that, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we show the B/C/S version as well so that we can see the whole seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you agree that it is a printed version of reports similar to those that you saw on the disk, the electronic version?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Of course without all of the handwritten notes and the stamp.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you know that for the whole year of 1994 for the northern site there are lists, existing lists, of archived material, of reports similar to this one with a seal.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we show the witness Exhibit 5D182.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did you ever have the opportunity to see the list of archived material, material such as this list here?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I agree with the -- with the Chamber's recommendation to redact the sentence. I did want to point out, though, that I think if my learned colleague could be more specific with respect to the list that she's referring to, because I do notice that the ones that are displayed pertain to a period of time in 1994. I know that the witness is testifying about material received in 1995. I don't know if it's her contention that such lists were maintained during that period of time, but I thought she could put that question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but in answer to her previous question and the stamp there, which was a stamp which goes back to 1994, in any case. So let's redact from line 12 on page 52, please, to line 17. Did you follow, Madam Frease, did you follow the exchange at that took place between Mr. Vanderpuye -- okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, fine. Go ahead, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I apologise. I really forgot about the unit that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: So you never saw such a list for 1994, neither for the northern site nor for the southern site, nor for the unit that belonged to the 2nd Corps and the other unit of the northern site?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall seeing such lists.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And you did not see either reports bearing a seal. However, I would like to ask you to look at Exhibit 5D194. I would request that this exhibit not be broadcast. You can see on the exhibit that it refers to the month of May, 1995, and it does bear a seal.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could we call up the last page of the document. And you see the date on this page, on the seal, is the 20th of May, 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We need to redact -- we need to redact that, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps could we move to private session, because I'm having too much difficulty here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Let's move to private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This report is dated the 1st of May, 1995, and has a seal, and it comes from Sector South. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And if you look at the last page. Could we turn to the last page, please. Is it fair to say that this report is dated 22nd of May, 1995?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, though the "5" in the handwritten stamped version is not terribly clear. But certainly the typed version from the southern site does say 22 May 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that at the time you scrutinised the material you had, including the printouts and the electronic versions, you did not know that this version of the reports existed? These hard copies containing a seal I mean.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. And also the time period. I mean, we were really focused on July of 1995. We started off looking at a week in particular. You know, somewhere from around the 9th of July to the 16th of July. And then as we worked through that material, then we expanded the dates a little bit more until we were able to finally cover all of July. And then we started to work a bit into August. And then the priority, as I recall, was to work back to June and then to September. So, yeah, May wasn't a real priority. But it is correct that I was not aware of these types of documents with stamps on them.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Don't you find it strange that reports that are dated the month of May contain a seal, whereas those documents dated in the month of July contain no seal?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not necessarily. I think there can be different explanations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We don't want you to speculate. If you are aware of explanations, then please go ahead, but if you are just speculating on what the explanations could be, then I don't think we need to hear that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My understanding is that we have electronic reports from July -- sorry, January 1995 through December, and perhaps more, and those that electronic copies would be the same versions of material that we've been referring to in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: As you focused on June and July, more specifically July 1995, how come you had the electronic version in January?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there was a misunderstanding. I believe we have the electronic versions of the conversations from January through December 1995, the seven diskettes that were received by the Office of the Prosecutor in December 2000.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I feel that a hard copy which contains a seal, and particularly if you were entitled to consult archive -- archived material, don't you believe that this is more authentic than material that had been recorded after the war?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree with the second part of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You said a while ago that the diskettes you got were copies of the files that had been created during the war. Do you know when these copies were made?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know specifically when they were made, but the first two diskettes were given to me in May of 1999.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In other words, these diskettes could have been created any time between July 1995 and May 1999?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you know that there was an SDB document that also contained a seal?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown Exhibit number 5D160, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let me see the document before it is broadcast, if at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This is a seal which largely resembles the seals we've seen in the other documents; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No broadcast, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: The only thing is it's a -- first line in this seal is handwritten, SDB. It could be a 2 because this document comes from the SDB. So that's more likely, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You mentioned on the 2nd of March, 2007, on page 19, you said that in certain areas Italian words were used instead of B/C/S in certain areas. Are you able to establish distinction between various B/C/S dialects?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends. I'm certainly no expert, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the Dalmatian, in so-called -- you described it that way, Dalmatian dialect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and the Serbian/Croatian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can you establish -- are you able to recognise specific Croatian words which were introduced again in the 1990s?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: One comes to mind. A couple come to mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Very well. I think the best would be to show you the conversation I'm interested in. It's Exhibit number P1195, 1195B. 1195B. Can the witness be shown the entire B/C/S version, please. Can you see after the third hyphen there's a word here, "Bojovnici." Do you know what this means?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You didn't hear that this word is used solely by Croatian soldiers belonging to the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: When you analysed the intercepts, you were helped by interpreters and translators, were you not?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And nobody drew your attention to the fact that it is highly unlikely that a VRS officer would have used such a word, which is only used by Croatian army soldiers, and all the more, this word has a particular meaning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: First, I don't think there's been any testimony in the record that that is language that's specifically used by Croatian military.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Fauveau is suggesting that, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'll agree with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- and not knowing any of the words except "Da" and "Ne," "Dobro." I cannot confirm or deny what she's suggesting.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The second half of that is that she's already answered the question, and that is that she's not heard the word before. She's unfamiliar with the word, and therefore, obviously nobody's brought that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, not --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe not so obvious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not necessarily consequential. Maybe it was mentioned in the course of her consultations, but let's see what she has to answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The question -- I'll go faster than Madam Fauveau. It's been suggested to you that during your consultations nobody drew your attention to the fact that it's highly unlikely that a VRS officer would have used such a word, which is only used by Croatian army soldiers, and all the more, this word -- that this word has a particular meaning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could we now turn to Exhibit P2443, please. And to move on faster, this is a list of coded names that would have been use by the Republika Srpska army. You said on the 26th of February, 2007, on page 42 of the transcript, that this list was established on the basis of information that had been provided by other people. Did you use this list when you analysed the intercepts?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sometimes I referred to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You said it was always on -- still on the 27th of February, on page 30 of the transcript, that you did not use the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina as a source when you analysed the intercepts. Do you remember having said this?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in the context of a question that Mr. Zivanovic asked me about the authentication binder and whether -- why I didn't use information from the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina to confirm information contained within the intercepts. Is that the right context?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that the specific list was compiled together with members of the ABiH army?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't believe it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown Exhibit 5D191, please. Can we show the bottom of the first page, please. I would like the document not to be broadcast, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that in this note which was written by you, you wrote what -- what is about to follow: [Previous translation continues]... "[In English] Although a complete list was requested, none was provided. An officer from the Bosnian army," I will not call the name, "provided the following call signs as he recalled them."

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that members of the ABiH army helped you in establishing this list?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The list and the memo to which you are referring, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I want to make sure that this page is not being broadcast. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: The four names which are on this list are also to be found on the other list in Exhibit P2443, Panorama, Zlatar. Would you like me to show you the exhibit again, P2443?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the list of code-names?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you don't need to show it to me again. I can explain this very easily. When we were starting this project and this memo that you -- that you bring up of mine, maybe we could go to the first page to confirm the date, but I believe it was probably April of 1998, we had just received this material. It was all completely new to us, and so we asked whether they had any recollection of who some of the participants would have been or what these code-names meant and what locations they would have referred to. However, in the meantime, we received quite a large amount of captured VRS documents that confirmed this -- these code-names and the locations that pertained to the code-names, as well as having spoken with witnesses, cooperating witnesses, who were able to confirm this kind of information. So I don't think there's a contradiction between what I had said before and your question now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau, your two hours, 30 minutes are up. We've got two more Defence teams, and between them, they have required 50 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I fully agree, but when I said that I needed two and a half hours, I had not received the documents we received on Wednesday and Thursday. My initial estimate was based on this time. I gave two and a half hours. In the meantime, we've received a great number of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is a revised estimate you have given to the staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not used to arguing with counsel. I'm going to give you five minutes, and you have to finish in five minutes, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Could the witness be shown Exhibit P1182B, please and also Exhibit 2367B. Maybe it will be better to place it on the ELMO because these are conversations. Can we show the conversation which starts at 25 minutes past 10.00 p.m.? And the other document is a conversation which starts at 26 minutes past 10 p.m.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have a better copy of this conversation that starts at 22.26 in the material that I had with me from the first day. Is it -- may I refer to it instead of this other copy, because the last line and the first line of the next page are -- I'm just not sure that they're complete.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: No problem. You can refer to your own material. Could you tell me, looking at these two conversations, how come the conversation which starts at 22.25 starts, in fact, much later than the conversation which starts at 22.26? In fact, the page which is the first page in the 22.25 conversation, you will be able to find it on the second page of the conversation which starts at 22.26.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. And the reason for that is that these two conversations were recorded at the two different sites. The one that you reference at 22.25 was recorded at the northern site, and the one that you reference at 22.26 was recorded at the southern site. In this -- this is an example of where a -- the -- the --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Ma'am, I believe that the two conversations come from the northern site. Are you quite sure that one comes from the southern site? I'm not at all sure. I believe that both conversations come from the northern site.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to double-check. You might be right. But I don't think it changes the -- the substance of what I was going to say, which is that the reason -- the reason for this difference is that the person, the operator who began to record the conversation at 22.26 captured the conversation earlier than the operator who captured it at 22.25. So in fact it's only -- it's actually on the bottom of page 00804649 where you begin to see similarities between the two conversations. The last line of that conversation says, "Sto je prosli put to davao tamo", and that is the first sentence of the conversation that begins at 22.25 on 00779721. Does that answer your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Not really, because I don't understand how the conversation which started at 22.26, which is a minute later, could have started before the conversation which started at 22.25. I shall move on to another question. This conversation --

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's just a matter of if you look at your watch and I look at my watch and we both say what time it is right now, we might be off by a minute or two.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Isn't it fair to say that the equipment records the time automatically, that the recording machines have a time indicator on them, don't they?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau, please stop -- refrain from asking such questions. We're not talking about the equipment here. We're talking of the notebooks, and the notebooks did not have an automatic clocking system.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Was this particular conversation confirmed by any other piece of equipment?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you have independent equipment which would enable you to corroborate this? In other words, did you find any other documents which might corroborate this conversation?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Off of the top of my head, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you remember which kind of material this refers to? This is my last question. Do you remember what material this conversation refers to? When you look at the 22.25 conversation, it's X and X who speaks on the fourth sentence and then X who speaks on the fifth sentence?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that this refers to Josipovic, who I believe was a member of the Sarajevo Romanija corps, that it was a piece of equipment that was shared among the units. I don't remember the specific piece. It could have been a multiple rocket launcher or something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This brings your cross-examination to an end, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: A quick question to Ms. Frease before we break. I'm not sure whether we had that evidence before, but you're saying that most of the intercept operators relied on their personal watches to note down the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll have -- do you wish to start now, Mr. Josse, or after the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I don't mind, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's have a 25-minute -- is that sufficient, Madam Registrar? A 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: May it please Your Honours. Ms. Frease, I want to take you back, if I may, to the 25th of January of this year when you were giving your evidence, and to approximately page 6399 of the transcript. And at that point in time, you were commenting on tab 1 of the authentication binder, and you were describing how you had compared two different accounts of a conversation that took place on the 11th of July of 1995 between Generals Gvero and Gobilliard. I take it you remember that.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And if I may be permitted, I'm going to summarise what you said because it was quite a long time ago. Basically, you had two different sources for this particular intercept. The first was the conversation that had been recorded by the SDB, and it consisted solely of what General Gvero was saying, they being unable to hear what General Gobilliard was saying. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may just refer to my index. Do you -- it was the 1610 conversation, right, on the 11th of July? Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And you also had a second account from a Major Fortin who was working with General Gobilliard and he had summarised the conversation on behalf of General Gobilliard. That's also correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: What I'm a little curious about, Ms. Frease, is why didn't you go to the horse's mouth and confirm the conversation via General Gobilliard?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, though time was always a factor, but I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Would you accept that in fact General Gobilliard was asked about the conversation on the 8th of February of 1999 in a formal interview carried out in the Paris Court of Appeal at the behest of this Tribunal? Does that ring any bell at all?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And it's a fact that General Gobilliard is not on the list of witnesses in this particular case. My question is simple. Did you have any part in the decision as to whether or not he should give evidence in this trial, you personally?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's, if we may, look, please, at that particular conversation and see how else it could perhaps be verified. Could P1074 be put up on e-court, please. And it's the third page in English, and I'm going to take the witness and the Court to the summary that Major Fortin provided. That's it. We see, Ms. Frease, at approximately the point that you have marked 2 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we need the third page according to the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: That's the page, Your Honour. It's the third page of P1074. That's the page I want anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: We see it says: "If UNPROFOR troops were really targeted, then it was the BiH who fired on to them according to their old scenario." So that is obviously General Gvero speaking, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would appreciate it if the document could be shrunk down a little bit so I could see the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Yes. The numbers in the left-hand margin, please.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: It's number 2 or 3. It's -- you see what I'm referring to anyway.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. I would say it's number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: My apologies, and I accept that. It's right, isn't it, that this assertion by General Gvero can be supported by other documentation, thereby further verifying the intercept, and to this end, before you answer the question, perhaps you'd have a look at 6D45. This is a document that comes from a Lieutenant General Janvier dated the 10th of July of 1995. It's addressed, the Court will perhaps take it from me at the bottom of the page, to General Rasim Delic. And if we look at the first and the third paragraphs, we see that General Janvier is saying: "I was deeply shocked to learn of the Bosnian and Herzegovinian army hostile action against an UNPROFOR Armoured Personnel Carrier on the 8th of July in the afternoon, and I have to express my deepest indignation with regard to the murder of a Dutch soldier in the area of Srebrenica." Then for reasons of time I'll go on to the third paragraph. "Later on, the Dutch APC encountered a BiH barricade across the road and while driving over an obstruction, it was fired on and hit by a BiH grenade. One Dutch soldier was seriously injured and he was evacuated to Potocari but died of his wounds at 1625B." So if we go back to the note of the intercept that I'm asking you about taken by Major Fortin, does this document that's still on the screen help your verification of the intercept between Messrs. Gobilliard and Gvero?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I see the original document, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I'm not clear what you're referring to. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The letter, the notes that Major Fortin took.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Yes, back to P1074, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which page?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: The same as before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The same as before.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it's inconclusive.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Why do you say that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because a number of things could have happened between the 8th of July when General Janvier wrote that letter and the 11th of July when this conversation took place between General Gobilliard and General Gvero.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Okay. It was the 10th of July for what it's worth that General Janvier wrote the letter?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That he wrote the letter but it referred to events of the 8th of July, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Let me try in relation to another passage of this document. If we could go down same page to approximately number 6. We see it says: "UNPROFOR troops were most welcome on the BSA territory where they would be treated comfortably and would be completely safe." Could the witness please be shown 6D22. This, unlike the last document, is an original B/C/S document. If -- I'm working from a translation, Ms. Frease, because I don't read the language, and it's in fact -- this is a document, if I can summarise, from General Krstic to the VRS Main Staff and the Drina command corps dated the 9th of July, 1995. It's number 4 that I'd like to ask you to look at. Conduct of UNPROFOR forces. I'll read the translation I've got, slowly. "The UNPROFOR forces at the check-points in Slapovici village and Buci village surrendered fully to our forces with all their weapons and equipment and asked for our protection. Ten UNPROFOR soldiers from the UNPROFOR check-point in Buci village have been probably sent to and accommodated in Milici, while five soldiers from the check-point in Slapovici have been accommodated in Bratunac. UNPROFOR forces from the base in Potocari village did not intervene at the check-points or attack our forces." So my question is the same again. Does that document shed any light or support your verification of the conversation between Gobilliard and Gvero?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, not necessarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Explain, please.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mean it could, but the dates here too are -- they're two days off. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Sorry, do go on.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we could have the original notes again from -- that Major Fortin took juxtaposed against this document in English, the English version of the document that's currently on the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That I don't know if it is possible, but if it is possible, then I don't know what the accused are going to be able to look at, because if we have the two English text on the screen, there will be none in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: It's a slight failing, if I may put it like this, of the e-court system, Your Honour. There's no way round it as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Don't look at me much more because I'm not to blame for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, I said that with some trepidation, not blaming Your Honour, because simply, out of respect, you're the person to look at in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Do you need the translation of Major General Krstic's document?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I would just -- I would just note the same -- you know, the same issue. And I don't have a detailed knowledge or recollection of the events of the 9th of July and how and where UN forces surrendered to Serb forces, but a lot of things certainly could have happened and did happen between the 9th of July and the 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Am I -- am I barking up the right tree in these questions that I'm asking you? Was it part of your job to look at these documents and see if they in some way fit in to these conversations that you've been telling us about for many days now?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't like to say that you're barking up the wrong tree, but in the two examples that you've provided, they don't contain the type of information that I would have relied upon in order to confirm the material that was contained within the intercepts, because I don't believe that the material there is -- is really strong enough. I think I always tried to provide documentation that related very closely to the events that were being communicated in the intercepted material.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Let me try once again, then I'll move to another topic. Can we go to the second page now of Major Fortin's note. Yes. Between really 9 and 10, again we're back to General Gvero. It says: "He claimed that a great number of UN vehicles stolen by the BiH and still painted white were used against the BSA. He said he had no absolute knowledge of who the troops in the vehicles belonged to but drew the general's attention to the BSA reliable information that those were the BiH." And to that end, could you have a look, please, at 6D23, which whilst it's being got up on the screen, is a document not dissimilar to the last one from General Krstic to the Drina Corps command, Pribicevac forward command post dated the 10th of July, 1995, headed "Very urgent." There we have it in the B/C/S. It's number 3, Ms. Frease, that I'd like us to look at. Again, I will read it slowly. We now have the English up. "UNPROFOR conduct in the Srebrenica enclave from observation and surveillance of the situation in the Srebrenica enclave. We concluded that a number of UNPROFOR check-points on enemy territory have been taken by the Muslims who are using some of the weapons and other military hardware in operation against our forces." Same question: Wearing your analytical hat, are you able to comment on how that fits in with the passage from Major Fortin's note that I read to you a few moments ago?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you scroll to the -- well, first, the bottom of this document it says that it was received on the 10th of July, 1995; is that correct? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: It does at 2315.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the top of the document is dated --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: The 10th of July.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Yeah, I -- I don't have any specific information that the ABiH captured vehicles, and so when you refer to paragraph 3, the last sentence that says, "weapons or other military hardware," it's not clear to me that there's a direct connection between weapons and military hardware and the phrase that you referred to in the notes that Major Fortin took. But if we could again have the page of Major Fortin's notes that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: So this is the second page of his notes, please. Between 9 and 10.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't -- I can't make a link between those two points.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: All right. Let me move on briefly to one other thing I want to ask you about, and that's this -- could we have P1096A put up on the screen, please. Whilst this is being done, Ms. Frease, this is a note prepared by a MUP intercept operator of an alleged conversation between General Gvero and Radovan Karadzic on the 11th of July of 1995. Could I ask you, first of all, in general terms, what work, if any, you did in terms of analysis in relation to this particular intercept?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Aside from reading it and understanding the contents?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe that I included it in the authentication binder, but it's a -- it's a -- General Gvero is reporting to President Karadzic on a conversation that you had just had with General Nikolai that is -- reflects a conversation, as far as I remember, that General Gvero had with General Nikolai.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I accept that General Gvero had this conversation with General Nikolai. My specific question is: You did no work which would verify that this conversation was in fact between General Gvero and Radovan Karadzic, did you?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And for completeness sake, perhaps you could have a look at -- I think it's P1096B. Is that it? I may have the wrong number here. Scroll down, please. No, my fault. Perhaps it's P2374.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: And may I just refer to my index?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I've got no problem with that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry, 2374A, has it a letter?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Yes. A, I think, is the English. Next page, please. Yes, I'm sorry. I can see what I've done here, and it's my fault entirely. I think it would be more helpful if we went back to P1096A and scrolled on a couple of pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have a re-examination, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I anticipate a relatively brief one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is Ms. Frease going to be available tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I haven't spoken with her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm putting the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Scroll on, please. It's number 536 that we're after on this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. I do beg your pardon, Your Honour. I cut across a rather important conversation you were having.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm used to that, Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I was concentrating very hard on this screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Frease. It will only be for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Could you scroll on, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document has only one page.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: There is -- you've probably got it there, Ms. Frease, and we can do this a different way. There is a conversation about 20 minutes later which also is allegedly between General Gvero and President Karadzic on the same day. It's headed 536 in the -- by the MUP operator. Do you have that there?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but just to clarify, it's about -- you're referring to the 1610 conversation between General Gvero and Nikolai and then the one that follows it on the screen is the 1623, so 13 minutes later.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: My question referred to the 1623 conversation between Gvero and Karadzic and you dealt with that and said that you did no work to confirm one way or the other whether the person, my client, was speaking to was in fact Karadzic. And my last question is in relation to the same intercept -- beg your pardon, the intercept 20 minutes later, allegedly between the same two participants and my question is the same, any work in relation to that as to who General Gvero might have been speaking to?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you very much, Mr. Josse. Mr. Zivanovic. Please don't repeat any questions that you have already put during your 1 hour 42 minute cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am going to limit my questions to the documents that I received in the meantime. Further cross-examination by Mr. Zivanovic:

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Good day, Ms. Frease. I'm going to ask you to look at document 5D191, actually, that my colleague Ms. Fauveau has already shown to you. These are your personal notes from the 21st and 22nd of April, 1998, during your visit to the northern and to the southern location, and conversation with the staff of the B and H. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I would like you to look at the subtitle which says: "Summary of records relating to intercept traffic," and to look at item 2 there which begins with: "Took it upon themselves to extract the intercepts relating to the Srebrenica and compile them in a binder totaling more than 500 pages."

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask you to clarify one thing in the B/C/S language that you also understand, the word "kompilirati" indicates to take a large number of things or parts of a large number of things and putting them together into one whole. In that sense, was it -- was it how you used this word "kompilirati" in that sense in this document?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how I would interpret it here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Applied to the intercepts, I understand that the staff of the 2nd Corps took it upon themselves to take the existing reports on the intercepts, to separate them partially or completely, and to put them together in one document and then to make a binder of that numbering more than 500 pages. Is that how it was?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how I understood it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Thank you. Based on this and having looked at this binder, I saw, and you also said that in your testimony, that it was all printed on perforated paper. So it was one piece of paper that was coming out of the printer, and later it was cut, and then they had problems with copying because the last line was usually dark. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that. Not that the last line was dark, but that it was usually missing in the photocopying process.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Precisely. So looking at this binder, I saw that they're in one and the same place, on the same page even. There is an overlap of conversations from different places. To summarise, we had two locations, the northern and the southern one. There was one unit at the southern unit. At the northern one there were three units that were doing this work. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And now I see in this binder that you gave to us that on one page, for example, there are interlapping conversations between those units amongst themselves. Did you notice that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you could let me look at those pages, I'd be happy to try to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Yes. Can I just ask that the witness be shown precisely that. And now I'm going to let you know which. That is document -- that binder is there. I mean, we're not going to be able to look at it through the e-court or the electronic version, but we can only look at it on the ELMO. So I can just ask that you be given the binder, and I'm going to tell you which pages of the binder you would need to look at.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: This is 1D235. The pages where the intercepts are are marked by hand. You will see that. There's a small number in the upper right-hand corner. I think you know that.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I would like you to look at the page marked with the number 2, for example.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Two conversations are overlapping there. That one conversation is characteristic because it's written in block letters. We said whose conversations were transcribed exclusively and only in block letters as compared to other intercepts that were transcribed by some other units. Do you agree that here, on the same page, these two conversations are overlapping? Can I ask to have this page put on the ELMO, please. Then it will be -- so that it can be seen what I'm trying to say. You can see at the top of the page there is a conversation written in small letters, and beneath that there is a conversation transcribed in block letters, and it's characteristic for a specific organisation that also was doing that work. Can you confirm that? Here we have compiled various conversations, and one unique document was made compiling all of these conversations. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I wouldn't say that they're overlapping, and it may be a question of interpretation, but, yes, that there are two different sources contained within this binder, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: But -- but it's not the same, you know. If the conversations were separate, that would be clear, but because they were taken from different locations. But in this situation, they were put together. They were all put together in one document which we can see precisely by these printed pages. For example, the conversation of one unit was put together with the conversation of some other unit even though they are not the same in their original authentic version. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, and that's part of what made it difficult to understand the process, because we didn't -- we didn't understand all of these more subtle differences.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I noticed this on other pages as well, and I don't want to burden the Trial Chamber by enumerating all those pages that are done in the same or similar manner, that are compiled in that way, but I have noticed something else. Perhaps you can look at this previous document again, 5D191. Thank you. For now, we will not be needing the binder.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I could --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: No, no, no. Your personal notes. And you will see that on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let her finish what she was about to say.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it's just that the information was shared among the units. So that would be an explanation as to why these types of conversations would have been included in -- in this binder. If that helps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: But did you get notice? Were you told that this is how they put together the conversations but only the conversations that they shared amongst themselves? Surely they didn't tell you that that's what they did, so you needn't bother.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I remember it being a source of confusion for us that was clarified then later in interviews with the operators. The existence of this third unit at the site was something that we didn't know at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Thank you. But I wanted to ask you something else. On the basis of this paragraph, that would be 5D191, your personal notes, I reached another conclusion on the basis of this and that is that the personnel of 2 Corps did this in an agreement with you, that they did the compilation and the binder that contained the compiled conversation made of bits and pieces of conversations in agreement with you.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe it would have been specifically in agreement with me. I wasn't present during the March mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: On the basis of this paragraph, again, I don't know if you have it on your screen or not, but in the second sentence says that this binder was given to ICTY personnel during the March mission. You say that you were not there, but this means that it had been requested earlier so that this could be compiled, put together in a binder and then handed over to you during the March mission. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that there is an error in that note, that the binder was given to us in March. I believe it was given to us actually in April. Prior to the March mission, there was a mission to the area, I believe in January, the end of January, beginning of February 1998, in which we first made contact with the authorities of 2 Corps, the deputy commander, I believe, and we had meetings with them, and I believe it was the first time that we had contact with them, and I was present then. And it was at that time that we talked about our desire to have access to the intercepted material, other material that they had, and then it was at that point that a further mission was discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Thank you. I will ask you some specific questions about that, because you did not tell us about the January mission. But let me just remind you of an exhibit, 1D222. That's a certificate of the delivery of the establishment chart of the Drina Corps that was handed over to Mr. Ruez on the 3rd of March, 1998. And then the problem was because in that document we only had the organisational chart of the Drina Corps, and we did not have the radio report, and in the meantime, the Prosecution has been able to locate the radio reports, and they were indeed handed over to us. So it was handed over on the 3rd of March, 1998. In this binder that contains more than 500 pages, I found a document that is designated as 1D234. I'm sure you remember about this, because you've already seen this when I -- when I showed it to you on the 26th of February. Could you please look at 1D234.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is there anything in particular you'd like me to look at?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, here it is. That's precisely what I had in mind. This is the page that I wanted to look at. That's the same date, 3rd of March, 1998, and it is entitled "Report -- reports compiled through radio surveillance in the period between the 9th of July, 1995, and 31st of July, 1995." That document is contained in the binder that was shown to you. So can we then agree that this was not a mistake and that this binder had already been handed over to you in March 1998?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just really not sure. I think that we need to -- my -- my recollection is that -- that the binder was actually given over to the Office of the Prosecutor in April. It's possible that members of the Office of the Prosecutor saw the binder during the March mission the same way that they saw the notebooks and they saw the tapes, but I don't believe that we took possession of the binder at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I showed you the signature of Mr. Ruez who received both the radio reports and the documents on that day, but if you were right that on the 26th of April, that that was the date when the Tribunal received the documents, that is correct, and this is corroborated by a document that is designated 1D233. That is also contained in this binder. So Mr. Ruez took receipt of the documents on the 3rd of March. The Tribunal took receipt on the 24th of April. And you can see this right here on this list.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just -- I'm just not -- I'm not sure. Because if we could go back to the preceding document and see exactly what it says, because just before we change documents, the one that we're looking at right now dated the 3rd of March, 1998, says: "Reports of captured radio communications from -- during the period from 9 July 1995 to the 31st of July, 1995." So it is pretty specific. "RI" there stands for radio intercepts; right? So if we could go now to the previous document, I'm not sure that that document is that specific where Jean-Rene Ruez signed -- where his signature is at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, let us read it then. Does it say here in this text, does it say "radio reports"? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: On the basis of -- so he did take receipt of them on the 3rd of March.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: So that is correct. Let us move on to the document 1D233, document 1D233. That's not the one. I can give you the hard copy since there seems to be an error here. So perhaps you can put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go through this quickly, otherwise we'll leave it until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, this is the document. You can see here it's the date that you noted, the 24th of April, 1998, right here at the beginning of the document. You can see that for sure. It's the same ERN number. This document is also contained in this binder that has 550 pages. So can you confirm that this is indeed correct --

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Could you please -- my question to you is, do you know where this binder containing 550 pages was between the 3rd of March, 1998, until the 24th of April, 1998?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't account for the difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I think we have to leave it there because there is another Chamber who needs -- which needs to start at 2.15. We'll continue tomorrow. I anticipate that you will only be here for a few minutes tomorrow, Ms. Frease, and I thank you for bearing with us. Thank you. Have a nice afternoon, all of you. We stand adjourned until tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 6th day of March, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.46 p.m.,
